questions.question: In standard Ed25519 (RFC 8032), what is the length and structure of a signature?
options: 32 bytes: only s
questions.explanation: An Ed25519 signature is 64 bytes: a compressed curve point R followed by a 32-byte scalar s.

questions.question: Ed25519 is deterministic: what primarily determines the per-message nonce r?
options: SHA-512(prefix || message) reduced mod L
A fresh random number sampled uniformly mod L
The public key encoded as a scalar
The curve parameter d
questions.explanation: Ed25519 derives r from a secret prefix (from hashing the seed) and the message, then reduces mod the group order L.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'clamping' in Ed25519 key expansion?
options: Force the secret scalar into a safe form for the subgroup
Make signatures shorter by truncating the scalar
Make verification faster by precomputing inverses
Ensure the public key encodes x instead of y
questions.explanation: Clamping clears/sets specific bits of the hashed seed so the scalar has the right structure for safe scalar multiplication.

questions.question: Which equation does Ed25519 verification check (conceptually)?
options: s·B = R + H(R, A, M)·A
s·B = H(M)·A
R·B = s + H(A, M)
A = H(R, M)·B
questions.explanation: Verification recomputes the challenge hash H(R, A, M) and checks the curve relation sB = R + kA.

questions.question: In Ed25519 point compression, what is stored directly in the 32-byte encoding?
options: The y-coordinate plus one bit of x
The x-coordinate plus one bit of y
Both x and y in full
Only an x-coordinate (Montgomery u)
questions.explanation: Ed25519 encodes y (255 bits, little-endian) and stores the parity of x in the high bit.

questions.question: Attack scenario: what happens if two different messages are signed with the same nonce r in an EdDSA/Schnorr-style scheme?
options: The private key can be recovered from the two signatures
Only one of the two signatures will verify
The public key becomes invalid and decoding fails
Nothing serious; nonce reuse is harmless in EdDSA
questions.explanation: Nonce reuse makes the equations share r, which lets an attacker solve for the secret scalar using basic algebra.

questions.question: Why is it important to bind a context / domain separation string into what you sign at the protocol layer?
options: It prevents cross-protocol replay of valid signatures
It makes signatures probabilistic instead of deterministic
It prevents all timing side channels in software
It removes the need to validate public keys
questions.explanation: Domain separation ensures a signature intended for one protocol message can't be reused as a valid signature for a different protocol message.

questions.question: Why must an implementation reject signatures where s is not in the canonical range (s >= L)?
options: To avoid accepting alternative encodings of the same signature
Because s would otherwise overflow 32 bytes
Because R decoding requires s < L
Because the curve equation changes when s is large
questions.explanation: Rejecting non-canonical s avoids signature malleability via multiple encodings representing the same group element.
